subject: Film & Cinema
title: Science Fiction's Big Questions
description: A short lesson to help you apply Science Fiction's Big Questions.

hook.text: Sci-fi asks 'what if?' and then follows that question to its most unsettling conclusion.

buildup.text: From Metropolis to The Matrix, sci-fi uses technology to explore human anxieties.

discovery.text: The genre's real subject is never the tech — it's always about humanity's relationship with it.

twist.text: Many sci-fi predictions have come true — surveillance, AI, genetic engineering.

climax.text: Science fiction is the genre that prepares us for a future we can't yet see.

punchline.text: Sci-fi is prophecy disguised as entertainment.

quiz.question: What is the true subject of most science fiction films?
options: Humanity's relationship with technology and change
